examples: Failover during primary AZ outage
Continuous availability for critical applications
Maintaining database uptime during maintenance
explanation.additionalInfo: Deploying Amazon RDS in multiple Availability Zones ensures that the database remains available in case of hardware or AZ failures. AWS automatically handles replication and failover, providing resilience and fault tolerance.

explanation.summary: AWS DMS is for data migration, not for providing high availability.
explanation.why: DMS helps move databases to AWS or between databases, but does not manage HA or failover for a running RDS instance.

questions.question: What is the MOST secure way to store passwords on AWS?

options.text: Store passwords in an Amazon S3 bucket.

explanation.summary: Storing passwords in S3 is insecure if not encrypted and lacks rotation management.
explanation.why: S3 is object storage and while it can encrypt objects, it does not manage secrets lifecycle or enforce access controls specifically for sensitive credentials.

options.text: Store passwords as AWS CloudFormation parameters.

explanation.summary: CloudFormation parameters are visible in templates and do not provide secure password storage.
explanation.why: Storing passwords as parameters can expose them in template files or console, lacking proper rotation and secret management.

options.text: Store passwords in AWS Storage Gateway.

explanation.summary: Storage Gateway is for hybrid storage, not secret management.
explanation.why: It does not provide secure, managed credential storage or rotation capabilities.

options.text: Store passwords in AWS Secrets Manager.

explanation.summary: AWS Secrets Manager provides secure, managed storage for secrets including passwords.
keyPoints: Integrates with AWS SDKs and services
examples: Storing database credentials for RDS instances
Rotating API keys for applications automatically
Managing passwords for service accounts securely
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built for secure storage and management of sensitive information such as passwords, API keys, and tokens. It ensures encryption at rest, controlled access, and automated rotation, providing best practices for security and compliance.

questions.question: Which statements accurately describe the relationships among components of AWS global infrastructure? (Choose two.)

options.text: There are more AWS Regions than Availability Zones.

explanation.summary: There are more Availability Zones than AWS Regions.
explanation.why: Each AWS Region contains multiple AZs, making AZs more numerous than Regions.

options.text: There are more edge locations than AWS Regions.

explanation.summary: AWS has many edge locations to deliver content closer to end-users.
keyPoints: Edge locations provide low-latency content delivery
Used by services like CloudFront and Lambda@Edge
Number exceeds the number of Regions
examples: Serving CloudFront content from multiple edge sites globally
Lambda@Edge functions executing near users for low latency
explanation.additionalInfo: Edge locations are part of AWS global infrastructure designed for performance optimization and low-latency delivery of content and applications. They outnumber Regions to maximize user proximity.

options.text: An edge location is an Availability Zone.

explanation.summary: Edge locations are separate from AZs and are used for caching and content delivery.
explanation.why: Edge locations do not provide compute or storage resources like AZs; they are designed for CDN and latency optimization.

options.text: There are more AWS Regions than edge locations.

explanation.summary: Edge locations outnumber Regions.
explanation.why: Regions are geographic clusters of AZs; edge locations exist worldwide to improve performance and are more numerous.

options.text: There are more Availability Zones than AWS Regions.

explanation.summary: Each Region contains multiple AZs, making AZs more numerous than Regions.
keyPoints: AZs are isolated locations within Regions
More AZs than Regions exist globally
examples: US East (N. Virginia) has multiple AZs
Deploying applications across multiple AZs for HA
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Regions are geographical areas containing multiple AZs. This structure allows for redundancy, high availability, and fault tolerance.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides DNS resolution?

explanation.summary: CloudFront is a CDN and does not provide DNS resolution services.
explanation.why: CloudFront relies on DNS but is not itself a DNS service.

explanation.summary: VPC provides networking isolation but does not provide DNS resolution for external domains.
explanation.why: VPC can host internal DNS but does not serve as a public DNS service.

explanation.summary: Amazon Route 53 is AWS's scalable and highly available DNS service.
keyPoints: Performs DNS resolution for AWS and external domains
examples: Resolving [www.example.com](http://www.example.com) to an EC2 instance IP
Routing traffic based on user location for performance optimization
Configuring failover DNS for disaster recovery
explanation.additionalInfo: Route 53 is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service designed to route end users to Internet applications by translating names like [www.example.com](http://www.example.com) into numeric IP addresses.

explanation.summary: Direct Connect provides dedicated network connections but does not provide DNS resolution.
explanation.why: It establishes private connectivity to AWS, but domain name resolution is not part of the service.

questions.question:
A company needs to host an application in a specific geographic area to comply with regulations.

Which feature of the AWS global infrastructure will help the company meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: Scalability is about adjusting resources to demand, not geographic location.
explanation.why: While AWS resources can scale, this does not ensure compliance with geographic data residency requirements.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Six Advantages Of Cloud

explanation.summary: AWS Regions provide physical locations to host resources in specific geographic areas.
keyPoints: Regions correspond to specific geographic areas
Enable compliance with data residency and regulatory requirements
Support low-latency access for users in that region
Isolated from other Regions for fault tolerance and compliance
Allows deployment of applications within a chosen jurisdiction
examples: Deploying servers in the Frankfurt Region to comply with EU data laws
Hosting financial applications in a country-specific Region
Ensuring healthcare data stays within a regulated geographic boundary
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS global infrastructure provides multiple Regions worldwide, allowing customers to choose where their applications and data reside to meet compliance and legal requirements.

explanation.summary: Availability refers to uptime, not geographic placement.
explanation.why: High availability ensures resources remain operational but does not guarantee compliance with location-specific regulations.

explanation.summary: Performance relates to latency and throughput, not regional compliance.
explanation.why: Although deploying closer to users can improve performance, it does not directly address regulatory data residency requirements.

questions.question:
An ecommerce company plans to move its data center workload to the AWS Cloud to support highly dynamic usage patterns.

Which benefits make the AWS Cloud cost-effective for the migration of this type of workload? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: Reliability improves uptime but does not directly reduce cost.
explanation.why: While reliability ensures consistent service, cost-effectiveness comes from resource elasticity and pay-as-you-go pricing.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Six Advantages Of Cloud

explanation.summary: Security is essential but does not directly make workloads cost-effective.
explanation.why: Securing workloads is necessary but savings are realized through elasticity and pay-per-use pricing.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Six Advantages Of Cloud

explanation.summary: Elasticity allows scaling resources up or down according to demand, reducing costs for variable workloads.
examples: Scaling EC2 instances during peak shopping hours
Adjusting database throughput for fluctuating query loads
explanation.additionalInfo: Elasticity is a core benefit of the AWS Cloud for workloads with highly variable demand. It ensures that the company pays only for the resources needed at any time.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Six Advantages Of Cloud

explanation.summary: Pay-as-you-go allows companies to pay only for what they use, optimizing costs for variable workloads.
keyPoints: Billing is based on actual usage
examples: Paying for EC2 instances only when they are running
Using Lambda and paying per invocation
Storage billed based on actual GB consumed
explanation.additionalInfo: Pay-as-you-go pricing combined with elasticity makes the AWS Cloud cost-effective for dynamic workloads by ensuring that resources are used efficiently and billed accurately.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Six Advantages Of Cloud

explanation.summary: High availability improves uptime but does not directly reduce cost.
